fact: The sky's second-brightest star — a distant beacon so steady that spacecraft steer by it.
bio: Canopus (Alpha Carinae) is a rare yellow-white bright giant roughly 310 light-years away, intrinsically thousands of times more luminous than the Sun. Its brilliance and position far from the ecliptic make it an ideal fixed reference — Mariner and later probes carried 'Canopus star trackers' to hold their bearings in deep space.
cultural: Often linked to a helmsman of the Greek fleet at Troy, Canopus is 'Agastya' in Indian tradition — a revered sage of the southern sky. Too far south for much of Europe, it was a prized season- and latitude-marker for navigators of the southern seas.
